papers.title: Collinear and Coplanar Altermagnetism in a Penrose Quasicrystal
papers.summary: We generalize the previous group-theory based classification of collinear magnetism in the quasicrystal (QC) to general magnetic states. Taking the Penrose lattice as an example, we find that all magnetic states belonging to 2D irreducible representations (IRRPs) of the $D_5$ point group, including collinear states and coplanar ones, correspond to altermagnetism (AM). Unlike conventional collinear AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flip the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are always mutually orthogonal. Taking the single-orbital Penrose-Hubbard as an example, our linear-response theory based calculations show that the largest portion of the parameter space is occupied by these 2D-IRRP states, and our further Ginzburg-Landau theory based analysis reveals that the polarization directions of the two basis magnetic states in the 2D IRRPs can be either parallel or perpendicular, leading to collinear or coplanar magnetic states. The special group-theory-orthogonality compensation mechanism and the absence of the PT symmetry finally leads to AM states, which are to be verified by the spin split in the spin-dependent angle-resolved-photoemission-spectrum and the spin conductance. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM can also emerge in other QCs.

papers.title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
papers.summary: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.

papers.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
papers.summary: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

papers.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
papers.summary: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

papers.title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
papers.summary: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.

papers.title: Anisotropic magneto-elastic coupling in the quasi-2D Ising magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ and thermodynamic signature of low-energy orbital excitations
papers.summary: The relevance of spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom in the quasi-2D Ising-like magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ is demonstrated by thermal expansion and specific heat measurements supported by numerical studies. By means of thermodynamic and Grüneisen analysis, we separate the orbital signatures and quantify the energy gap and its pressure dependence from the experimental data as $Δ\sim 300 - 350$ K and $\partial \ln Δ/\partial p_{\rm c} \approx -4.6$ %/GPa). Both values excellently agree with the theoretical DFT predictions. The thermal expansion anomalies associated with the onset of long-range magnetic order imply significant magneto-elastic coupling and are used to determine the anisotropic uniaxial strain dependencies of $T_{\rm N}$. They are dominated by the in-plane (i.e., $c$ axis) response $(\partial \ln{ T_{\rm N}} )/\partial p_{\rm c} \simeq 15$ %/GPa while the (negative) $a$ axis and (positive) out-of-plane ($b$ axis) pressure dependencies are much smaller. Short-range magnetic order extends well above $T_{\rm N}$ but is not driven by the same energy scale as $T_{\rm N}$ as evidenced by the observation of non-monotonic in-plane distortion, sign-change of the Grüneisen parameter, and failure of Grüneisen scaling.

papers.title: Orbital-selective correlations in kagome flat bands of Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
papers.summary: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal \CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level ($\EF$) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward $\EF$ driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near $\EF$, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at $\EF$, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.

papers.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
papers.summary: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$Sb$_x$ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with $x$ = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV$_6$Sn$_6$ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.

papers.title: Dynamic helimagnetism via charged spin current
papers.summary: We present a theoretical and numerical study of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons that carry both charge and spin currents, deriving the effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian. Applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain, these equations yield two current-driven helical phases: a static helix stabilized by a pure spin current alone, and a coherently precessing helix that appears once a small charge-current component is added. For a given helical wavenumber, the precession angular frequency $ω$ and the canting ratio $Δ$ toward the hard axis follow analytically from the equations of motion, while the wavenumber $q_{\rm helix}$ of the precessing helix is selected by a heuristically constructed effective Lagrangian. Direct numerical integration of the same equations of motion reproduces all three observables wherever it yields a coherent helix. The helix chirality is set by a long-range, current-generated Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM)-type coupling rather than an intrinsic DM interaction, so materials without bulk or interfacial DM interactions could also host current-controlled helical order. Because the helical pitch, precession frequency, and canting ratio are all continuously tunable by the current amplitudes, these helices could serve as probes of spin currents.

papers.title: Electronic Responses in Solid Oxygen with Coexisting Structural and Magnetic Orders
papers.summary: Solid oxygen provides a unique platform for studying the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom, as each O$_2$ molecule possesses an $S=1$ spin and weak intermolecular van der Waals interactions allow substantial structural flexibility. In addition, because of its small intermolecular hopping integrals, this system is known to be a strongly correlated electron system with a multiorbital nature. In this study, we examine electronic states and magnetic and dielectric responses using a multiorbital Hubbard model with Peierls-type electron-lattice coupling. This model provides a minimal description of the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom in solid oxygen. We apply the Hartree-Fock approximation to obtain the ground-state phase diagram. Antiferromagnetic order appears when the onsite Coulomb interaction is strong, whereas three nonmagnetic bond-ordered states emerge when it is weak. At intermediate interaction strengths, antiferromagnetic order coexists with each of the three bond orders. These three coexistence phases all break time-reversal symmetry; one preserves spatial inversion symmetry, whereas the other two also break it. The two inversion-breaking phases exhibit linear magnetoelectric responses, whereas the inversion-symmetric phase exhibits altermagnetic spin splitting and a piezomagnetic response. These responses may provide experimental signatures of coexisting magnetic and structural orders in high-pressure solid oxygen suggested by recent experiments.

papers.title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
papers.summary: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

papers.title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
papers.summary: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.

papers.title: Quasiparticle Interactions in the $S = 1/2$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnetic Chain CuPzN
papers.summary: We investigate spinon--spinon interactions in the quasi-one-dimensional $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet Cu(C$_4$H$_4$N$_2$)(NO$_3$)$_2$ (CuPzN) using inelastic neutron scattering. At zero field, the spectrum exhibits the canonical multi-spinon continuum of the Heisenberg chain. With increasing field we demonstrate the appearance of an energy gap $2Δ$ towards momentum $q\rightarrow 0$ between the uniform magnetization precession mode and the shifted spinon continuum. $2Δ$ is a direct measure of spinon backscattering interactions. Comparison with numerical matrix-product-state calculations and a recent analytical theory shows excellent agreement. By examining the integrable spin-1/2 chain, we provide an example of how quasiparticle interactions can be quantified experimentally in isotropic quantum spin systems.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
papers.summary: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.

papers.title: Theory of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau of the Spin-$1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet
papers.summary: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2π/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.

papers.title: Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry
papers.summary: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.

papers.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
papers.summary: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling $ρ=5/3$ and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, $T_{\mathrm{c}}=0.0314|U|$. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.

papers.title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
papers.summary: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/Å. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $Γ$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.

papers.title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet
papers.summary: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.

papers.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
papers.summary: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

papers.title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
papers.summary: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree--Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle--hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe--Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral $f$-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

papers.title: Second-Harmonic Bulk Response of Fractional Quantum Hall Fluids
papers.summary: We develop a bulk description for the second-harmonic Hall response of fractional quantum Hall fluids with broken inversion and rotational symmetries, distinct from edge theories based on nonlinear edge-mode dispersion. By projecting a tilted massive Dirac model onto a single low-energy band, we construct a composite-boson Chern--Simons theory for the lowest Landau level that retains projection-induced nonlinear electromagnetic couplings. The nonlinear Hall resistivity vanishes in the dc limit, while its finite-frequency response retains the characteristic filling-factor dependence $ρ^{(2)}_{TLL}\proptoν^{-2}$, where $ν$ is the Landau-level filling factor. At low frequency, its real and imaginary parts scale as $(ω/ω_c)^2$ and $ω/ω_c$, respectively, where $ω_c$ is the cyclotron frequency, and the response is strongly anisotropic with respect to the crystalline tilt axis. Notably, the Kohn-mode resonances present in the second-order conductivity cancel in the nonlinear Hall resistivity. These results establish finite-frequency nonlinear transport as a bulk probe of fractional quantum Hall fluids without requiring nonlinear edge-mode dispersion.

papers.title: Exact Magnetic Confinement of a Doped Hole by Kinetic Frustration
papers.summary: We establish an exact mechanism of magnetic confinement driven purely by kinetic frustration. In a finite open sawtooth $U=\infty$ Hubbard chain of $L$ unit cells doped with one hole, the ground state at magnetization $M$ contains $M$ polarized triplet dimers surrounding a connected singlet region of length $\ell_{\rm s}=L-M$. A magnetic field selects $M$ and hence the confinement length. The hole forms a standing wave in the singlet region with exponential tails in the triplet background. Confinement requires neither disorder nor an exchange-generated string tension: destructive interference between direct and apex-mediated hopping makes the triplet bonds reflecting. At $t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(π/(\ell_{\rm s}+2))]^{-1/2}$, they become perfectly reflecting, producing a position-degenerate compact localized state. At every fixed field $0<h<h_{\rm sat}$, the singlet region remains finite as $L\to\infty$ and shrinks stepwise with increasing field, whereas at $h=0$ it spans the system.

papers.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
papers.summary: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

papers.title: Cooperation of itinerant and localized physics in the magnetic phase diagram of 214 Ruddlesden-Popper iridates
papers.summary: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the Néel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.
